abstract: Poverty and mortality are the two major sources of well-being losses. We propose new summary indicators of well-being that account for mortality while being (i) conceptually sound, (ii) easily interpretable and implementable and (iii) sensitive to the distribution of well-being. Our main indicator is the poverty-adjusted life expectancy index. Following the expected life-cycle utility approach a la Harsanyi, it is based on a single normative parameter that transparently captures the trade-off between poverty and mortality. Empirically, we compare countries over time and focus on these situations in which mortality is in conflict with poverty. Once we assume that being poor is (at least weakly) preferable to being dead, we find that about a third of these conflicting comparisons can be unambiguously ranked by the poverty-adjusted life expectancy index. Finally, this indicator naturally defines a new and simple index of multidimensional poverty, the expected deprivation index, which also accounts for unequal lifespans.
abstract_zh: 贫困与死亡率是福祉损失的两大主要来源。我们提出了新的福祉综合指标，该指标在考虑死亡率的同时，具备以下特征：（i）概念严谨，（ii）易于解释与实施，（iii）对福祉分布具有敏感性。我们的核心指标是贫困调整预期寿命指数。遵循哈萨尼式的预期生命周期效用方法，该指数基于单一规范性参数，能够透明地反映贫困与死亡率之间的权衡关系。在实证层面，我们通过跨国时间序列比较，聚焦于死亡率与贫困存在冲突的情形。一旦假设贫困状态（至少弱）优于死亡状态，我们发现约三分之一的此类冲突比较可通过贫困调整预期寿命指数获得明确排序。最后，该指标自然衍生出一个新颖且简洁的多维贫困指数——预期剥夺指数，该指数同样考虑了寿命不平等问题。
title: A transparent index of well being accounting for mortality: Poverty Adjusted Life Expectancy.
title_zh: 考虑死亡率的透明福祉指数：贫困调整预期寿命
